Faṣl 1: On the conditions binding upon everyone

Among them is cleaving to the community; then sound belief, conformable to explicit unveiling; and perseverance in purity, both sensible and spiritual; then the training of thought in meditating upon the meanings of these names, by way of reflection and by way of inductive survey, such that there is generated from that perfect certainty, the knowledge of their secrets, and complete conviction as to the efficacious influence of them all; then the assumption of their character, as has been set forth above.

Then know, [all of] you, that whoever desires a universal operative deployment must needs assume the character of all the names, so that each name may give him what lies within its power. That is attained by divesting oneself of every attribute and by emptying the locus of every thing. So whenever he desires operative deployment by a name, he turns toward the Presence of that name, made ready to receive what comes upon him from it, by means of emptying the locus of the surplus of every thing — of lights and rays — so that there is in it no room for anything other than it; and thus he becomes identical with it in act and in operative deployment. And a universal operative deployment may be obtained through the assumption of the character of a single name, by means of one of two things. Either that name is among the universal roots; or else this assumption of character comes about through the inner sight's taking hold of the matter of witnessing in relation to the Presence of this name, such that he witnesses it without its comprehending and gathering within itself all the remaining names. And [so it is] with what is related of the shaykh Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Sabtī, of the perfection of operative deployment [that came to him] through his assuming the character of His name, exalted is He, al-Jawād (the Munificent) — so much so that he, may God the Exalted be pleased with him, used to say: From al-Jawād existence is acted upon. And with what is related of Abū Mūsā al-Sadrānī, that he had, as his litany in a day and a night, 70,000 complete recitations, through his assuming the character of God's name, exalted is He, Bāsiṭ (the Expander). And I have mentioned, concerning the assumption of the character of the names, a company — such as Abū al-Qāsim al-Qushayrī, Abū al-Ḥākim al-Barjānī, Abū al-Barakāt ʿAbd al-Qādir al-Jīlānī, Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī, Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ḥarrānī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh Ibn al-ʿArabī, Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Aqlīshī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Kūfī, and a multitude whose number none reckons but God, exalted is He. So let whoever wishes to gain acquaintance with it ponder that in their words. So understand that, for it is a confirmation of what has preceded. And know that the human being is himself the Greatest /fol. 123v./ Name of God; and whoever knows himself has known his Lord. And the shaykh Abū al-Ḥasan al-Shādhilī — may God be pleased with him — said: I was present before my shaykh ʿAbd al-Salām b. Mashīsh, and he had a small son, and I set him in my lap. Then I was minded to ask the shaykh about the Greatest Name, whereupon the boy took hold of my chin and then said to me: O uncle, you are the Greatest Name of God — or he said: the Greatest Name of God is within you.
So the shaykh said: He has answered you — meaning the boy. So understand.
Faṣl 2: On the conditions binding upon some and not others

Among them is the taking of pure metal for the engraving; and the seeking out of the time appropriate to the request; and fumigating with the fitting suffumigation; and the wearing of the particular garment. For all these are only conditions in respect of the weak, who have not attained the attainments of [true] men. And know that whoever stands at the degree of adhering to these stipulations must take a chamber for the litany of remembrance, in which he does nothing other than that, and in which no one else does anything either. And let its measure be the measure of what he needs for his sitting and his standing, nothing at all of it being in excess beyond him. There is to be in it no aperture through which [anything] may enter at all, and it is to be far removed from all sounds. He sits in it in direct contact with the ground, without any barrier; and if he has need [of something], then [let it be] of what the earth causes to grow. And he does not sleep save from being overcome [by sleep]; and he keeps up the fragrant suffumigations at most of his times.

*A subtle point (laṭīfa). One of them was asked about the meaning of withdrawal (ʿuzla), and he said: its very description announces its meaning, and its form gives tidings of what lies in its purport — that is, whoever chooses withdrawal, al-ʿuzla, then al-ʿizz lahu*, "might is his". And it is said: the [solitary] sitting is the loftiest of them. And know that the precious spiritual retreat is the bond of the people of election, and that withdrawal is among the signs of union. So understand that. And how excellent is the saying of him who said:
The house of sainthood (wilāya) — its pillars have been apportioned; our masters within it are of the Substitutes (abdāl):
between silence and unceasing withdrawal, and hunger, and wakefulness — pure and exalted.

And the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((Silence bequeaths the knowledge of God, exalted is He; withdrawal bequeaths the knowledge of this world; hunger bequeaths the knowledge of Satan; and wakefulness bequeaths the knowledge of the soul.))

I say: Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in obeying Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that the forebears (al-salaf), may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them, are agreed that the limit of the Lordly opening (al-fatḥal-rabbānī) and of the ṣamadānī unveiling is not attained save by one in whose stomach there is not the least trace of a mote of food; and that is the limit of corporeal self-sufficiency (al-ṣamadāniyya al-jismāniyya). And there has been disagreement about that: it is said that it comes about within two weeks; but the more widely held view among them is that it does not come about save with the completion of the 40 [days]. And that is what God, exalted is He, stipulated in the case of /fol. 124r./ His interlocutor Moses son of ʿImrān — peace be upon him — in the 40, so that his stomach might be purified of the grossnesses of foods, and thereby the spiritual being of his spirit grow strong, and his heart become clear, and his intellect grow strong, and his soul become wholesome. This, then, is the self-sufficiency of the spirits; and the forebears have set its limit at the end of the 60th day. And in it one apprehends the marvels of the dominion (malakūt), the subtleties of the omnipotence (jabarūt), and the secrets of the kingdom (mulk). As for the self-sufficiency of the intellects, by the totality of the human essence, it is 70 days; and that is the end of the period for those who undertake the spiritual discipline. And from it [comes] another genesis — that is, his interior grows up with lights of special election such as he had not known before, neither from the masters of the [mystical] states nor from the ranks of the deeds; and the secrets are unveiled to him, and the veils are lifted from his inmost secrets. And he it is who died through annihilation (fanāʾ) and was then brought to life through subsistence (baqāʾ). And this is the last rank of self-sufficiency within humanity, by the totality of the essence, in respect of its worlds and the kinds of its self-disclosures (tajalliyāt).

Know that the substance of the natural appetites is not cut off save after a complete hunger — thus has the ancient custom run in the secrets of the spiritual disciplines. As for the self-sufficiency of the natures, its limit is 28 days; and there is nothing less, for one who traverses the beginnings of the secrets of self-sufficiency, than a discipline of 14 days. As for the one upon whom the traces of habit stir within a week, they bind him to [the ordinary] means and bring him out of the retreats, because of their knowledge of the ruin of his interior in respect of the Lordly incomings and the gifts of faith. And some of them used to diminish his food each day by [the weight of] a date-stone; and among them is he who does not work at the lessening of the sustenance, but rather works at deferring it by degrees, until his gradation ends at 7 days, and 10 days, up to 40. And among them is he who alters his eating by a moist stick, diminishing his food every night by the measure of the drying of the stick. And Sahl said: whoever goes without food (ṭayy) for 40 days, power in the dominion (malakūt) is made manifest to him. And we have already disclosed the secrets of wayfaring (sulūk); so understand, and you will hit the mark. And let us seal this noble conclusion and subtle introduction with a rare litany of remembrance and a wondrous litany (wird), whose suns of meaning and subtleties of expression shine forth. This fragrant blossom and gleaming secret: God holds intimate colloquy by means of it with no servant but He sets him free; nor with any captive but He releases him; nor is there any prisoner but he is delivered, nor any man in fear but he is made secure, nor any poor man but he is made rich, nor any abased man but he is made mighty. And in it is a marvellous meaning for the crushing of tyrants and the cutting off of the last remnant of the wrongdoing folk. And whoever writes it and hangs it upon himself, every obstinate tyrant and rebellious satan is abased before him; and no one sees him but loves him. And whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God gives life to his interior with the light of the gnoses and to his exterior with the spirit of the subtleties, and guards him in his family and in his own self, and suffices him against the evil of what you fear. /fol. 124v./ And no king makes remembrance of it but his kingdom is enlarged and his word takes effect. And in it is the Greatest Name of God. And whoever recites it before a tyrant at the time of his anger, his anger is stilled; and he does not ask God, exalted is He, for a need but He gives him what he asked. And whoever knows how to turn [to God] (tawajjuh) by this hidden secret and treasured pearl is dispensed thereby from many of the operative litanies of remembrance of this kind. And it has a spiritual retreat [devoted] to it, which the masters of inner sight know; and the litany of remembrance for it is the All-Comprehending Name, for the greatest of those enraptured [in love], and Ḥayy Qayyūm (Living, Self-Subsisting) for the masters of the beginnings. And were a man to wish to give clear expression to the secrets of this radiant ruby and dazzling emerald from the side of its numerical secrets, its letter-borne effects, its luminous names, and its dispositions in awfāq, he would be wholly taken up with the arduousness of it. And it behooves kings, princes, viziers, the righteous, the most excellent of the scholars, and the most skilled of the sages to turn [to God] by it in the first [hour] of the day of Friday, or the day of Sunday, or the day of Monday, or the day of ʿArafa, or the day of the two feasts, or the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, or the eve of mid-

Shaʿbān, or the eve of the 27th of the month of Ramadan, or at the new moon of every month, or on the nights of all time; and that is after a prayer of 6 salutations. And when he sits at the end of it, let him say: Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is greatest, and there is no power and no strength save in God, the Exalted, the Mighty. O God, bless the Prophet Muḥammad, and his family, and his wives — the mothers of the believers — and his progeny and the people of his house, as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham; truly You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. Then let him pronounce the takbīr and prostrate himself; and let him say, while prostrate, Fātiḥat al-Kitāb 7 times, and the Throne Verse 7 times, and "There is no god but God alone, who has no partner; His is the kingdom and His is the praise, and He is powerful over every thing" 10 times. Then let him say: O God, truly I ask You by the bonds of might from Your Throne, and by the utmost reach of mercy in Your Book, and by the right of Your name, the Magnificent, the Greatest, and Your highest majesty, and by Your perfect words. And after that let him ask for his need. Then let him raise his head and give the salutation to the right and to the left. Then, if it be possible, let him slaughter a fat ram, free of defects, in an empty place, with a lawful slaughtering, turned toward the qibla; and let him say at the slaughtering: O God, this is from You and unto You. O God, truly it is my ransom, so accept it from me. And let him dig a pit for it and fill it in with earth; and let him cut it into 60 portions — the hide a portion, the head a portion, the right side a portion — and distribute it among the poor and the destitute, and feed 60 destitute persons with the most excellent of food; or let him give in alms 7 dirhams to 7 destitute persons. So understand; for the gates have been opened for whoever wishes to enter. And God bestows His bounty upon whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of magnificent bounty. And He is the Granter of success. /fol. 125r./

And this is the litany, magnificent in measure. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. And there is no power and no strength save in God, the Exalted, the Mighty. And you say: O God, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham among the worlds; truly You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. And you say There is no god but You. Glory be to You! Truly I was among the wrongdoers (Q 21:87) 126 times. And you say God suffices me; there is no god but He. Upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne (Q 9:129) 7 times. And you say: I ask forgiveness of God, beside whom there is no god, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, and I turn to Him in repentance — 3 times. And you say: In the name of God, with whose name nothing in the earth nor in the heaven can do harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing — 3 times. And you say "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord (Q 36:58) 16 times. And you say: There is no power and no strength save in God, the Exalted, the Mighty — 10 times. And you say: O Wadūd (the Loving), O Wadūd, O Possessor of the Glorious Throne, O Mubdiʾ (the Initiator), O Muʿīd (the Restorer), O Doer of what He wills. I ask You by the light of Your face, which has filled the corners of Your Throne; and I ask You by Your power, by which You have power over the whole of

Your creation, and by Your mercy, which embraces every thing: there is no god but You. O Mughīth (the Succourer), succour me — 4 times. And you say: O ʿAlī (the Exalted), O ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent), O Walī (the Protecting Friend), O ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), O Ḥannān (the Tender), O Mannān (the Bounteous), O Raḥīm (the Compassionate), O Raḥmān (the All-Merciful), O Jamīl (the Beautiful), O ʿAṭūf (the Ever-Kindly), O Ḥamīd (the Praiseworthy), O Raʾūf (the Ever-Gentle): I ask You by Your name that is hidden in the knowledge of Your treasured Unseen, that You pour out upon me, from the outpouring of Your most holy beauty and Your most precious perfection, a luminous secret and a lordly name, that I may deploy it operatively upon souls and bodily forms, life-bloods and spirits, with the stirrers of love and the stirrers of affection. O You by whom is the relief of the sorrowful, and the intimate companion of the desolate: I ask You by the secret of the bent alif (al-alif al-maʿṭūf), which is the origin of the letters. O Wahhāb (the Bestower), O Nāfiʿ (the Bringer of Benefit), O Tawwāb (the Ever-Relenting), O Rāfiʿ (the Raiser): [grant me] a longing that will bring me to You, and a light that will guide me to You; and receive me with repose and fragrance, and gladden me with security from You and with [Your] good pleasure. I ask You, O Bāsiṭ (the Expander), O Wāḥid (the One), O Mājid (the Glorious), O Wājid (the Finder): God, God is my Lord; I associate nothing with Him. O God, whoever intends against me evil, or harm, or ill toward me — subdue his might, tie up his tongue, bridle his mouth, restrain his guile, and come between me and him. O Dāʾim (the Everlasting), O Ḥamīd (the Praiseworthy), O Mujīb (the Answerer), O
Majīd (the All-Glorious): by the sanctity of Muḥammad, Muḥammad, Muḥammad, Muḥammad, Muḥammad, Muḥammad, Muḥammad.

O God, truly I ask You by the all-comprehending secret and the shining light, that You bestow upon me a criterion (furqān) from You, whereby my breast may be expanded and my worth raised. You are my direction and my standing, and unto You is the return and the ultimate end. You mend the broken and break the tyrants. There is no god but God, the Magnificent, the Forbearing. There is no god but God, Lord of the Mighty Throne. There is no god but God, Lord of the seven heavens and of the earth and of what is between the two, and Lord of the noble Throne. O God, God of Jibrīl and Mīkāʾīl and Isrāfīl and ʿAzrāʾīl, and of Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac: grant me well-being, and set none of Your creation over me with anything for which I have no strength. O Hearer of the invocation, /fol. 125v./ O Answerer of supplication! So He will suffice you against them, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing (Q 2:137). I have put my trust in the Living who does not die. Praise belongs to God, who has taken no child, and who has no partner in sovereignty, and who has no protector out of abasement; and magnify Him greatly (Q 17:111). God is greatest, God is greatest, God is greatest — mightier than the whole of His creation. God is greater than whatever I fear and whatever I guard against. And I take refuge in God, other than whom there is no god, who holds back the heaven from falling upon the earth save by His leave (Q 22:65), from the evil of every obstinate tyrant and every rebellious satan. O God, truly I ask You for security from rejection, and security from being driven away, and security from poverty, and security from blame, and security from anxiety, and security from grief, and security from abasement, and security from ignorance, and security from the [evil] eye, and security from being swallowed up by the earth, and security from the quaking of the earth. O God, make good our final outcome in all matters, and grant us protection from the disgrace of this world and from the punishment of the hereafter. O God, truly I ask You by Muḥammad, the perfect lord, the opener, the seal, the light of the lights of the gnoses and the secret of the secrets of the bestowed graces (ʿawārif), the choicest of Your creation, the secret of Your knowledge, the mirror of Your Essence, and the witnessing-place of Your attributes; and I ask You by the light of Your Face, and by the carpet of Your mercy, and by the seven and the eight and their secrets that are joined [in unbroken succession] from You. O God, O God, O Aḥad (Unique), O Ṣamad (Eternal Refuge), O Ḥayy (Living), O Qayyūm (Self-Subsisting): bestow upon me, from Your knowledge, knowledge and action and intellect; and from Your life, a spirit; and from Your will, a decree; and from Your power, an act; and from Your words, a tongue; and from Your hearing, understanding; and from Your sight, unveiling; and from Your encompassment, a standing firm. And grant me, from You and through You, a secret before which the necks of the arrogant shall bow low and to which the souls of tyrants shall be led in submission. For to You belongs praise, O Barr (the Benign), upon every beginning; and to You belongs thanks, O Bāqī (the Everlasting), upon every ending. Truly You are al-Mughnī (the

Enricher), al-Majīd (the All-Glorious), and al-Ghanī (the Self-Sufficient), al-Ḥamīd (the Praiseworthy). My God, lay me down upon the bed of Your mercy by Your favour, and keep watch over me with the watchman of Your safekeeping and Your preservation; and wrap me in the mantle of awe (hayba), and seat me upon the couch of magnificence, crowned with the crown of resplendence; and pitch over me the pavilion (surādiq) of safekeeping, and unfurl over me the banner of might; and fill my inward with reverent fear and mercy, and my outward with magnificence and awe; and give me mastery over the forelock of every obstinate tyrant and every rebellious satan; and preserve me from error and from slipping, and strengthen me in word and in deed. O God, truly I ask You by You, and by what Your Essence comprises of that which none knows but You — of You I ask that You bless the Muḥammadan Essence and the subtle unitary reality (al-laṭīfa al-aḥadiyya), the sun of the heaven of secrets and the place of manifestation of the lights, the pole of the sphere of Beauty and the centre of the orbit of Majesty. O God, by his secret with You and Your secret with him: give security to my fear, and pardon my stumbling, and take away my covetousness and my sorrow, and make complete what is deficient in me, and take me to Yourself away from myself, and provide me with annihilation (fanāʾ) in You away from myself; and do not make me one infatuated with my own soul, veiled by my sense-perception; and unveil for me every concealed secret, O Ḥayy, O Qayyūm; and suffice me in that with a subtle kindness (luṭf) in which the spirits of the friends of God (awliyāʾ) find rest and for which the souls of the felicitous are made eager. For to You belongs the most ample glory /fol. 126r./ and the most all-embracing kingship.

O God, truly I ask You by every name that has gone before in Your knowledge — truly You refuse no petitioner who asks by it, and You turn away disappointed none who asks You by it — I ask You to fulfil my need in that wherein I am Your poor one, and to accompany me in that with goodly well-being. Truly You know what I desire; with You are the keys of all affairs, and You are powerful over all things. O God, truly I ask You by the secret of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" that You pour out upon me, of the raiment of Your lights, that which shall send back the eyes of the enemies abased and their hands in loss; and that You clothe me, in everything I undertake, with a splendour from You in which the spirits of those who perceive find rest, upon which the eyes of the beholders are fixed in wonder, and by which the innermost secrets of the gnostics are gladdened. Truly You are the All-Knower of hidden things and their Teacher, the Unveiler of secrets and the One who gives understanding of them. To You belongs praise and laudation, and in Your hand are the triumph and the opening. O God, bless Your prophets and the messengers, and Your angels brought near, and Your righteous friends, and all the people of Your obedience; and convey to them our peace and our greeting, and bring us their intercession, together with our request and our wish. O God, truly I have turned my hope toward Your noble Face, and I have thought well of Your mighty pardon; so have mercy upon me, and have mercy upon my parents and upon those who turn [in repentance] to me, and make well pleased with me those who turn [others] away from me and who set themselves against me; and do not turn my hope away from Your Face disappointed, and do not make my good opinion of Your pardon a lie. My God, how should I depart from Your door in disappointment, when I have loved it in confidence in You? And how should You leave me bereft of Your bestowal, when You have commanded me to call upon You? O most merciful of the merciful! O Lord — when my appointed term has run out, and my work is cut off, and I have put on my shroud and parted from my dwelling: O Lord of lords, O Causer of causes, O Setter-free of necks, O Remover of torment: the harm of my own soul has touched me, so have mercy upon me, for You are the most merciful of the merciful. In the name of God, al-Shāfī (the Healer). In the name of God, al-Kāfī (the Sufficient). In the name of God, al-Muʿāfī (the Restorer to Health). Alif-Lām-Mīm-Rāʾ. Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād. Ṭāʾ-Sīn. Ḥāʾ-Mīm. Qāf. Nūn. God is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful (Q 12:64).

Then you say "There is no god but God" 100 times, and you say Yā Laṭīf 129 times, and you say Yā Kāfī 111 times, and you say Yā Ḥalīm (O Forbearing) 88 times. [Those secrets] which none may attain save the single ones among the masters of secrets and the singular ones among the masters of lights — and none is granted it save those who have been patient, and none is granted it save one possessed of great fortune (Q 41:35). So ponder this red sulphur and this greatest theriac, and there will gleam for you a flash from the science of the names and the letters, and the secrets of the numbers, and the meanings of the receptacles (ẓurūf). And you say Yā Mujīb 55 times, and you say Yā Salām (O Peace) 131 times, and you say Yā Ḥafīẓ (O Preserver) 998
